//: Headers and routing only. The build settings — root directory, install
and build commands, output directory — live in the Vercel dashboard, and
duplicating them here would mean two places to change and one of them

rewrites.//: Client-side routing: /new and future /c/:slug are React Router paths, not files. Vercel checks the filesystem before rewrites, so real assets still serve themselves.

headers.//: Cross-origin isolation, which is what makes SharedArrayBuffer available. The simulation worker shares the statevector with the main thread through one; without these two headers it falls back to copying transferable buffers, which is slower but works — the app checks crossOriginIsolated rather than assuming.

require-corp is only safe because the app loads nothing cross-origin: the three fonts are self-hosted precisely so this holds. Adding any external resource later means giving it CORP headers or losing SharedArrayBuffer.
Vite fingerprints everything under /assets, so a URL there can never change meaning.
